# Codex kickoff — do not edit production UI yet

Use `$orange-art-direction`, `$orange-paper-genesis`, `$orange-signal-login`, and `$orange-motion-qa`. Read `design/ART_DIRECTION.md`, `MOTION_SPEC.md`, `ASSET_MANIFEST.md`, `QA_GATES.md`, and `REFERENCE_BRIEFS.md`; view all reference images/SVG storyboards. Read the canonical project specification and inspect the actual working tree. We are rejecting the previous static-background + floating DOM implementation entirely as an art direction. Preserve all functional server-side logic, forms, validation, email/OTP, roles and security. Do not erase the old design until a reviewed replacement is ready; operate in an isolated branch or worktree if supported.

**First deliverable only: G0–G2, a standalone local motion lab.** Before coding, show proposed keyframes and asset approach; if art references are not approved, stop at G1. Do not rewrite Register.cshtml/Login.cshtml or add database migrations. Once art is approved, build a standalone local prototype with editable 2D paths and actual Three.js geometry (or Blender-generated GLB) with physically connected folds, named scene nodes, same geometry coordinate system and timeline. The original 2D scene must genuinely start flat and progress to actual 3D at the company stage. No stock/generated photo backdrop, no floating DOM stickers, no unrelated image swaps. Use a labelled development panel for replay, scrubbing (0–100%), reverse, category switches, orbit/wireframe proof. Login is a single telecom hardware assembly: SIM pads, precise circuit traces, fiber cable, physical aperture; no network cliché. The fingerprint is visual-only disabled. Lab controls must be fictional and separated from real auth. Do not invent biometric or OTP success.

Run a local browser. Provide real screenshots at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% across the main transforms; desktop and mobile; short recording of the actual browser animation and a 3D orbit demonstration. Document tested device/runtime and actual performance observations. Inspect the frames yourself before reporting. If required model authoring or visual capture is blocked, stop and explain rather than creating a lower-quality substitute. No real customer data, OTP or credentials in screenshots/logs.

Stop after G2 and request explicit visual approval. Do not integrate until I approve. Provide changed files, actual evidence paths, known shortcomings, and next steps. A build alone is not acceptance. The objective is visual quality and continuity, not the quantity of code generated.
